note: Three mathematically distinct candidates for #111, each frozen with the campaign's proposal schema. This is a DESIGN: no implementation exists, no CGV gate has been run, and the cgv_gaps field records exactly where the current verifier cannot yet check the declared mechanism. Nothing here authorises a GPU run.

proposals.title: A product-hyperbolic level-0 quantiser with separately supervised factors
proposals.equation: j*(z) = argmin_{j=1..256} [ d_{c}^2( exp_0^c(s_s * z[0:16]),  exp_0^c(a_j) ) + d_{c}^2( exp_0^c(s_b * z[16:32]), exp_0^c(b_j) ) ]; d_c(x,y) = c^(-1/2) * arcosh( 1 + 2c||x-y||^2 / ((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2)) ); zhat = [ log_0^c(exp_0^c(a_{j*})) ; log_0^c(exp_0^c(b_{j*})) ]; grad(a_j) = sum_i w_s * d(L_recon + beta*L_commit)/d(a_j); grad(b_j) = sum_{(i,i') in T} w_b * d(L_trans)/d(b_j)

symbols.z: the host encoder's 32-dimensional output, the tangent vector at the origin
symbols.z[0:16] / z[16:32]: the two declared 16-dimensional halves; the split is fixed and orthogonal, so it cannot rotate away later
symbols.a_j / b_j: the j-th level-0 codeword's tangent coordinates in the semantic / behaviour factor (16 numbers each); the ball point is exp_0^c(a_j)
symbols.c: the curvature magnitude of BOTH factors, fixed at 1.0 at specification time; the metric is the product of two Poincare balls of curvature -1
symbols.s_s / s_b: the fixed tangent scales of the two factors, 0.5 and 0.5, declared so the probe latents sit inside the ball with a recorded boundary margin
symbols.d_c: the Poincare geodesic distance of curvature -c
symbols.exp_0^c(v): the exponential map at the origin, tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)/(sqrt(c)||v||) * v, whose image always satisfies c||x||^2 < 1
symbols.log_0^c(x): the inverse exponential map at the origin
symbols.j*: the level-0 code the item is assigned; the ONLY change to the SID export's construction
symbols.L_trans: the train-only transition term: -log softmax_j( -d_c(exp_0^c(s_b*z_i[16:32]), exp_0^c(b_j)) / tau ) at j = j*(successor of i)
symbols.tau: the transition temperature, fixed at 0.25 at specification time

domains.manifold: B^16_{-1} x B^16_{-1} (a product of two Poincare balls, each of curvature -1)
domains.points: items and codewords are tangent vectors at the origin; every ball point is exp_0 of a tangent vector, so c||x||^2 < 1 holds by construction and no projection is needed
domains.tangent_domain: the ambient R^16 per factor; the metric tensor at x is g(x) = (2 / (1 - ||x||^2))^2 * I
domains.distance: the product distance is the sum of the two factor geodesic distances squared; the total sectional curvature is not constant
domains.boundary: the declared boundary margin is 1 - ||x||_max recorded at probe time; a candidate that saturates tanh (||v|| > 8) is reported, not clamped

proposals.why_hyperbolic: The assignment is the argmin of a sum of two geodesic distances in two Poincare balls, so the Voronoi cells of the 256 joint codewords are hyperbolic Voronoi cells, whose boundaries are not the Euclidean bisectors: two codewords at the same Euclidean distance from a point can be at different geodesic distances, and the disagreement grows with ||x||. Removing the curved metric and using ||x - a_j||^2 changes which codeword is nearest for points near the boundary, which is the mechanism, not a decoration.
proposals.role_assignment: The two factors are NOT left symmetric: the semantic factor's codewords receive only the reconstruction and commitment gradient (content), and the behaviour factor's codewords receive only the train-transition gradient (behaviour). The split is declared and masked in the backward, so identifiability is structural, not learned. Both factors participate in the joint assignment, so the L1 code is chosen by content and behaviour together and neither alone can move it.

gradient_paths.L_recon + beta*L_commit: reaches a_j only (the b-half is masked with a zero multiplier in the same backward)
gradient_paths.L_trans: reaches b_j only (the a-half is masked identically)
gradient_paths.encoder: reaches the encoder through the straight-through estimator of the assignment and through the commitment term, unchanged from the host

sid_effect.L1: the assignment changes; this is the mechanism's whole effect on the export
sid_effect.L2_L3: unchanged: levels 1 and 2 of the host's residual chain quantise zhat, the tangent decode above, exactly as before
sid_effect.protocol: 3 tokens per item, 256 codes per level, 32-dimensional budget: the joint codebook still holds 256 codewords of 16+16 numbers

compatibility.dimensions: 32 = 16 + 16; the factor split is a fixed orthogonal partition of the same 32 coordinates, so no budget is added
compatibility.capacity: 256 joint codewords (NOT a 256x256 product): the pairs couple the factors, which is exactly why this is not classical product quantisation
compatibility.export: unchanged integer schema; levels 2 and 3 are the host's

hypotheses: the product geodesic assignment gives the level-0 codebook cells that are anisotropic near the ball boundary, so the L0 tail (largest cell, distinct codes) changes for the same 256 codes without the transition pairs having to collide more

because the two factors are separately supervised, the behaviour term can shape the L1 partition without moving the content factor's geometry, so the transfer failure of Case A/E (a coarser L1 partition bought by the behaviour objective) is not forced
the joint assignment is dominated by neither factor: for a nontrivial share of items the two factors' nearest codewords disagree, and the joint argmin follows the sum
expected_failure_modes: boundary saturation: if the probe's latents have ||z|| >> 1/sqrt(c) after the declared scale, tanh saturates and every point crowds the boundary, which collapses the geometry toward a rescaled Euclidean assignment and makes H3 fail
vacuous split: if the joint assignment agrees with the semantic factor alone for >= 99% of items, the behaviour factor carries no decision and the mechanism is inert
codebook collapse: the transition term can pull a few b-codewords onto the dominant successor geometry, reducing the effective L0 alphabet
capacity loss in the tail: the anisotropic cells may trade a smaller largest cell for more singleton cells, which would show as a falling distinct-code count without any downstream change

tests.statement: log_0^c(exp_0^c(v)) = v within 1e-6 for 8 synthetic tangent vectors at c=1 and at c=2
d_c matches the closed form, is symmetric, is zero only on equal points, and satisfies the triangle inequality on 16 random triples
on fixed points and codewords, the assignment changes for at least 5% of the probe when c is doubled, and the disagreement with the Euclidean nearest codeword falls monotonically as c -> 0
the reconstruction+commitment backward leaves the b-half's .grad exactly zero and the transition backward leaves the a-half's .grad exactly zero, without any detach on the geometric path
the joint assignment equals the semantic-only assignment for strictly fewer than 99% of the probe items and of one real train batch
the pooled level-0 codebook gradient equals the independent mean of the four ranks' local codebook gradients within 1e-5
the exported SID has exactly 3 tokens per item, every token in [0,255], and the L0 histogram uses more than one code

proposals.differentiation: Not SAHL: no PCA, no whitening, no K-means, no Euclidean subspace block, no occupancy cap, and 3 tokens rather than 16-64 digits. Not Gu et al.: the product manifold is the quantiser's assignment metric with a role split, not a representation. Not Switch Spaces: no learned gate and no per-input choice of space. Not HVQ-VAE: two factors with separately masked supervision, not one hyperbolic codebook.

prior_art.r8_07_hyperbolic_gyro_translation: a Mobius/gyro TRANSLATION of points; this candidate does not translate any point, it changes the metric under which a codebook is assigned
prior_art.r8_08_hyperbolic_frechet: a Frechet BARYCENTRE of successors used as a target; this candidate takes no barycentre of anything
prior_art.r8_09_hyperbolic_radial_hierarchy: a per-layer RADIAL reweighting of the hierarchy; this candidate has no radial term and no per-layer weight
prior_art.r8_10_hyperbolic_gw: a graph-code Gromov-Wasserstein matching; this candidate solves no transport problem between graphs
prior_art.sahl_2026: PCA blocks (whiten=True) + K-means + balanced residual quantisation over sentence embeddings, K=16..64 digits. This candidate has no PCA, no K-means, no Euclidean subspace block and 3 tokens
prior_art.gu_2019_product_spaces: a product of constant-curvature factors as a REPRESENTATION; this candidate uses the product as the QUANTISER's assignment metric and its gradient's role split
prior_art.switch_spaces_2021: sparse learned gates over product components, no quantisation; this candidate has no gate module and no per-input space switch
prior_art.hvq_vae_2025: a single hyperbolic codebook for images; this candidate has two factors with separately supervised codewords

proposals.falsifier: The candidate is refuted if, on the probe and on one real train batch, (a) the joint assignment agrees with the semantic-factor-only assignment for >= 99% of items, or (b) the L0 largest cell does not fall below the control's 237 while the smallest cell does not empty, or (c) the L2/L3 tokens change at all (the mechanism must be confined to level 0).

predicted_consequences.ER: prediction: rises less than the Case A/E arms did, because the behaviour factor cannot coarsen the content partition; a rise of +0.3 to +0.6 with a largest cell at or below the control's is the informative outcome
predicted_consequences.G_H1: prediction: unchanged or slightly up at matched L0 occupancy; a rise accompanied by a falling distinct-code count is the Case C artefact and refutes the mechanism's usefulness
predicted_consequences.D2: prediction: no claim; the conditional level-2 support in this cohort is too thin to order arms
predicted_consequences.Recall_NDCG: prediction: the first plausible route to a joint movement, because the L1 partition keeps its content geometry while the transition structure lives in the other factor; a repeat of Case B (a clean ER gain with no downstream movement) refutes the hypothesis

mechanism.summary: the level-0 assignment minimises a sum of two Poincare geodesic distances with separately supervised factors

cgv_gaps: G5: the current non-trace branch measures the ENCODER gradient only and sets the codebook deviation to NaN, so verify_encoder_and_codebook_gradients is honoured by the trace branch and not by the non-trace branch. The declared target here is the codebook, so G5 does not yet verify this mechanism's own gradient; the engine needs the codebook pooling in the non-trace branch before an executable claim is made.

G2: the declared expected_paths describe the HOST's loss terms (base nonzero, behaviour zero). The factor mask makes the half-specific path invisible to G2; it is covered by the p1_factor_mask test instead, which is a mechanism-specific check, not a CGV gate.

G3: mode is 'invariants' (finite, nonzero). A formula-mode G3 would need an independent oracle for the product-geodesic gradient; oracles.assemble_gradient has no rule for an additive term of this shape (the same limitation the R10 arm hit at G5).

proposals.title: A codeword-frame residual chain: parallel transport of the level-0 residual before quantising levels 2 and 3
proposals.equation: x = exp_0^c(s * z)  (the item's ball point, log_0^c(x) = s*z the tangent); a = exp_0^c(a_{j*})  (the assigned level-0 ball point); r = PT_{x -> a}( s*z - log_0^c(a) )_a  (the residual, transported into the codeword's tangent frame); levels 2 and 3 quantise r with the host's Euclidean codebooks; zhat = log_0^c(a) + PT^{-1}_{a -> 0}( r_hat )  where r_hat is the level-2/3 codeword sum

symbols.z: the host encoder's 32-dimensional output (tangent at the origin)
symbols.x / a: the item's and the level-0 codeword's Poincare ball points, curvature -1
symbols.a_{j*}: the assigned level-0 codeword's tangent coordinates (the host's codebook, unchanged)
symbols.PT_{x -> y}(v): parallel transport of the tangent vector v from x to y along the unique geodesic, an isometry of the tangent spaces under g
symbols.r: the transported residual, expressed in the tangent frame AT the codeword; this is what the level-2 codebook sees instead of z - log_0(a)
symbols.r_hat: the level-2 and level-3 codeword sum, quantising r
symbols.zhat: the reconstructed latent fed to the host's decoder and used for the RQ commitment

domains.manifold: B^32_{-1} for the item point and the level-0 codeword; the tangent space at the codeword is where the residual lives
domains.points: every point is exp_0 of a tangent vector, so the ball constraint holds by construction
domains.tangent_domain: T_a B^32 with the metric g(a) = (2/(1-||a||^2))^2 I; the transport is an isometry between T_x and T_a
domains.distance: the level-0 assignment is the host's Euclidean assignment (UNCHANGED); the geometry enters only through the transport of the residual
domains.boundary: the transported norm equals the source norm exactly (isometry), so the near-boundary behaviour is a large norm in T_a, which is reported, not clamped

proposals.why_hyperbolic: Parallel transport along a geodesic of the Poincare ball is not the identity and not a linear map of the ambient space: it mixes the radial and tangential components with a factor that depends on the ball metric at both endpoints. The residual that levels 2 and 3 quantise is therefore a genuinely codeword-relative object, and the ambient residual (z - log_0(a)) is a different vector. Without the curved metric there is no transport: a Euclidean PT is the identity, so removing the geometry removes the mechanism entirely.
proposals.role_assignment: Level 0 keeps the host's partition (the semantic/behaviour assignment is untouched, which is testable as bit-identity). The factorisation is between the LEVELS: level 0 fixes the frame, levels 2 and 3 carry the residual inside that frame. This is #111's Family D question (one SID whose levels coordinate) answered with a manifold transport rather than with a new token alphabet.

gradient_paths.L_recon + beta*L_commit: reaches the level-0 codebook through zhat's dependence on log_0(a) and on r_hat's transport
gradient_paths.level_2_3_codebooks: receive the reconstruction and commitment gradient in the transported frame
gradient_paths.encoder: reaches the encoder through the straight-through estimator of the level-2/3 assignment and the commitment term

sid_effect.L1: bit-identical to the host (declared and tested)
sid_effect.L2_L3: change: they now index the transported residual, so the same L2/L3 code means a different displacement depending on the L1 codeword
sid_effect.protocol: 3 tokens, 256 codes per level, 32 dimensions: unchanged

compatibility.dimensions: 32 throughout; no split of the latent and no extra parameters beyond the host's
compatibility.capacity: 256 codes at every level; the L2/L3 codebooks still hold 256 x 32 numbers

hypotheses: the ball metric stretches distances near the boundary, so the ambient residual z - log_0(a) under-states displacements for items far from the origin; transporting it into the codeword's frame makes the residual's norm equal the geodesic distance up to the first order, which should reduce the level-2 quantisation error for exactly those items

because the residual is codeword-relative, the level-2 codebook can spend its 256 codes on local displacements instead of a global one, which should raise the L1->L2 branch count without changing level 0
the effect is curvature-caused: as c -> 0 the transport tends to the identity and the mechanism must converge to the host
expected_failure_modes: no-op: on probe latents with small ||z|| the transport is nearly the identity, so the level-2 assignment is unchanged and the mechanism is inert
near-boundary blow-up: for ||x|| close to 1 the transport's factor grows, and the L2/L3 gradient norms can become large; the test records the maximum and the declared margin

frame inconsistency: if the level-2/3 codebooks learn a codeword-dependent frame while the decode inverts it incorrectly, the reconstruction loss rises and the arm is an implementation failure, not a mechanism failure

tests.statement: ||PT_{x->y}(v)||_{g(y)} = ||v||_{g(x)} within 1e-6 for 16 random (x, y, v) at c=1
PT_{y->x}(PT_{x->y}(v)) = v within 1e-6
when the codeword is the origin the transport is the identity, and as c -> 0 the transported residual converges to the ambient residual
the L1 token of every item is bit-identical to the host's export on the same checkpoint
with the level-2/3 codeword sum set to zero, zhat equals the host's tangent decode log_0(a) within 1e-6
the level-2/3 codebooks receive a finite nonzero gradient, and the level-0 codebook still receives one through the commitment path
the pooled level-2/3 codebook gradient equals the independent mean of the four ranks' local gradients within 1e-5
3 tokens per item, every token in [0,255]

proposals.differentiation: Not R8-07: gyro-translation moves points, this transports a residual's frame. Not R8-08: no barycentre. Not R8-09: no radial reweighting. Not R8-10: no optimal transport between graphs. Not any Euclidean residual-transport arm (r8 / #107 / #109): their residual is ambient, and a Euclidean parallel transport is the identity, so those arms are exactly the c -> 0 limit of this one and are falsified as distinguished by this test.

proposals.title: A metric-aware conflict gate: the behaviour gradient is projected against the content gradient in the codeword's own Riemannian metric
proposals.equation: at each level-0 codeword a_j: g_j = (2 / (1 - c||exp_0^c(a_j)||^2))^2 * I; <u,v>_R = u^T g_j v;  conflict iff <g_beh, g_rec>_R < 0; if conflict: g_beh <- g_beh - ( <g_beh, g_rec>_R / (<g_rec, g_rec>_R + eps) ) * g_rec; the gate is applied to the codeword parameters only, and only on the coordinates of the behaviour half

symbols.g_j: the Riemannian metric tensor of the Poincare ball at the codeword's ball point, a scalar multiple of the identity whose scale depends on ||exp_0(a_j)||
symbols.g_beh / g_rec: the behaviour term's and the reconstruction term's gradient with respect to the level-0 codeword parameters
symbols.<.,.>_R: the inner product induced by g_j; a positive-definite but position-dependent inner product
symbols.behaviour half: the declared last 16 coordinates of the level-0 codebook, where the behaviour term is allowed to act

domains.manifold: B^16_{-1} per factor for the codewords; the metric tensor is evaluated at the codeword
domains.points: the codewords are the host's Euclidean codewords, mapped by exp_0 for the metric evaluation only; the assignment stays Euclidean, so the export's construction is unchanged in kind
domains.tangent_domain: the codeword's tangent space with g_j = (2/(1-||x||^2))^2 I
domains.distance: none used: the mechanism is a gradient-level gate, not a distance
domains.boundary: the metric's scale diverges as ||x|| -> 1; the declared margin and the maximum scale are recorded, and the gate is skipped (declared) when the scale exceeds 1e6

proposals.why_hyperbolic: The conflict set is defined by a position-dependent inner product. Two gradient pairs with a negative Euclidean dot product can have a positive Riemannian dot product near the boundary and vice versa, so the set of coordinates that get projected differs from Euclidean PCGrad's, and the difference is caused by the curvature. As c -> 0 the metric becomes the identity and the gate degenerates to Euclidean PCGrad, which is the declared control.
proposals.role_assignment: The behaviour half of the codebook is the only place the behaviour gradient may act, and the gate decides whether it is projected there. The factor split is thus enforced by the gradient's support, and the curvature decides the projection.

gradient_paths.L_recon: the level-0 codebook's content gradient, unchanged
gradient_paths.L_trans: the behaviour gradient on the last 16 coordinates, projected when the Riemannian inner product is negative
gradient_paths.encoder: unchanged from the host (declared zero change)

sid_effect.L1: changes only where the projection fires

compatibility.verdict: comparable with the frozen protocol; train-only, so the export changes only through the learned codebook

hypotheses: the curvature makes the conflict set position-dependent, so near the boundary the gate fires on a different set of codewords than Euclidean PCGrad would, which changes which codewords the behaviour term is allowed to move

if the Case A/E failure is a gradient conflict at the codeword, gating the behaviour gradient in the codeword's own metric should keep the L0 tail (largest cell) at the control's while the transition share still improves
as c -> 0 the mechanism must reproduce Euclidean PCGrad's update exactly, which is a falsifiable identity, not an assumption
expected_failure_modes: overlap: the projected set equals the Euclidean one for all codewords on the probe, making the metric cosmetic
inert: the reconstruction and behaviour gradients rarely conflict at the codeword, so the gate never fires
scale blow-up: near the boundary the metric's scale makes the projection coefficient tiny or huge; the declared skip threshold and the recorded maximum are the guard

tests.statement: g_j is symmetric positive definite with a positive determinant for 32 sampled codewords
as c -> 0 the projected coordinate set converges to Euclidean PCGrad's, and at c=0 the update is bit-comparable within 1e-9
for at least one codeword with ||x|| above 0.5 the Riemannian conflict sign differs from the Euclidean sign on the same gradient pair
after projection the Riemannian inner product of the two gradients is >= -1e-9
the encoder's gradient is identical to the host's within 1e-9 on the same batch
the pooled codebook gradient equals the independent mean of the four ranks' local gradients within 1e-5

proposals.differentiation: Structurally this is the R4-08 conflict-projection family, which is the honest overlap: it projects one gradient against another. The difference is the metric: R4-08 and every #109 tangent-rotation arm project in the ambient Euclidean inner product, and this candidate projects in g(x) = (2/(1-c||x||^2))^2 I, whose scale depends on the codeword. It is therefore NOT offered as a novel mechanism; it is the cheapest diagnostic of whether the ball metric changes the conflict structure at all.

cgv_gaps: G5: same non-trace codebook gap as P1 and P2.

selection_procedure: The three act on three different loci: P1 on the level-0 assignment metric with separately supervised factors; P2 on the residual frame between level 0 and levels 2-3; P3 on the gradient's metric at the codeword (train-only). They are not three settings of one idea.

SAHL already does it (verified, Euclidean), and #111 forbids it as a subspace mechanism
breaks the frozen 3-token protocol; #111 §4 Family D asks for one SID

rejections.reason: changes the capacity and is classical product quantisation
R8-08 already owns the Frechet barycentre operator
that is #110's current R10 arm; a second arm on the same operator would duplicate #110's registry

rejections.reason: invalidated after freezing by the geometry review: the Poincare metric is conformal (g = lambda(x)^2 I), so the PCGrad coefficient is invariant and the projected vector is identical to r4_08's Euclidean PCGrad. Measured conflict-set disagreement 0.0 over 256 codewords. See subspace_geometry_review.json F2. The proposal is kept as the record of a hypothesis that was tested and refuted before implementation.
